newsitem.title: CHILE: Australia's AMP to examine Ecuador/Mexico minerals.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP to examine Ecuador/Mexico minerals.

text.p: Inversiones Mineras Los Andes, a joint venture between Chile's state copper company Codelco and the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), said it is to study copper and gold deposits in Ecuador and Mexico.
"We are going to look at some offers of gold deposits in Ecuador to see if they are worth pursuing or not," Los Andes general manager Nicolas Saric told Reuters.
The properties in Ecuador include unexplored deposits and more advanced sites where drilling has been carried out, he said.
Los Andes is interested in developing deposits with reserves of at least one million ounces of gold, said Saric.
In Mexico, the company has been offered sites with gold and copper reserves, he said.
The company, which was set up last year, will present the results of its prospecting at four properties in Chile to a board meeting at the end of the month, he said.
"We have finished the first studies at the sites which will be presented to the board in July," said Saric.
Los Andes is 51 percent owed by AMP, with the rest held by Codelco, the world's largest copper producer.
The AMP-Codelco deal is one of a series of joint ventures Codelco has signed with foreign private companies, the biggest of which is the El Abra copper mine with Cyprus Amax Minerals .
